title: This Month's figure and trend line both include today's sales
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in on the build under test as an Admin user. The Admin role holds every permission, including Reports. To use another role, first check Settings > Roles & Permissions > that role: the Reports permission must be on.
  2. Pick one workplace in the workplace selector at the right of the top bar (e.g. QA Testing).
  3. Use a desktop browser at 100% zoom on a screen at least 1024 pixels wide (any ordinary laptop or desktop monitor).
  4. Open the Dashboard and write down the Revenue headline on This Month (e.g. $2,422.00).
  5. Then create one invoice dated today, with no discount, using these steps:
    • Customers > New Customer, enter a name (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer") and save.
    • Work Orders > New Work Order, pick that customer and an asset (use Add in the dialog if the customer has no asset), then Create.
    • In the work order header set the service advisor (e.g. Marcus Halvorsen).
    • On the Lines tab click New Line and add a labor line with labor hours (e.g. 1.00) and a price (e.g. $250.00), and assign a technician to the line (e.g. Grace Sullivan).
    • Sign in as that technician in a second browser, clock in on that line, and clock out after a known time (e.g. 15 minutes, which is 0.25 hours). Sign out of the second browser.
    • Back as Admin: approve the line, complete the work order and click Review.
    • Open the Finance tab and click Create Invoice. The invoice is dated today. Close the payment dialog that opens.
  6. Nobody else creates an invoice or a credit memo in this workplace while you run the case (if you cannot be sure, write that in the result comment).
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top bar.
  2. Read the Revenue headline (pill on This Month).
  3. Look at the right-hand end of the Revenue trend line, where the line ends in a dot.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The Revenue headline has gone up by exactly the invoice's $250.00 (e.g. $2,422.00 + $250.00 = $2,672.00), so the This Month figure runs from the 1st of the month up to today.
  • The trend line ends at today: its last point (the dot at the right-hand end) has risen compared with before the invoice, so the same partial window, 1st of the month to today, is shown by the line as by the headline. Exact point values cannot be read off the small trend line by hand; pass or fail on the rise you can see.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9579 (Story 7, Per-Tile Date Ranges); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 7. Split out of C88618 so each case checks one thing.
